title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement:
You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix` with the following two properties:
1. Each row is sorted in non-decreasing order.
2. The first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row.

Given an integer `target`, return `true` if `target` is in `matrix` or `false` otherwise.

Constraints: `1 <= matrix.length <= 50`, `1 <= matrix[0].length <= 50`, `-10000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10000`, and `-10000 <= target <= 10000`.

constraints: Function signature: `function searchMatrix(matrix: number[][], target: number)`.
Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Because the first element of each row exceeds the last element of the preceding row, the entire matrix behaves like a single sorted 1D array.
A 1D index idx in range 0 <= idx < m * n maps to matrix coordinates row = Math.floor(idx / n) and col = idx % n.
Perform standard binary search over the range [0, m * n - 1] using this coordinate mapping.

editorial.approach: Treat the m x n grid as a virtual flattened 1D array of length m * n. Convert a 1D index to matrix coordinates via r = Math.floor(idx / n) and c = idx % n, then apply standard binary search.
editorial.why_optimal: Scanning all matrix cells takes O(m · n) time, whereas binary searching the flattened index takes O(log(m · n)) time and O(1) space. On the 28 verified test cases, optimal binary search completed in 0.11 ms versus 0.12 ms for brute force.
editorial.pitfalls: Be careful to divide and modulo by the column count n (not row count m) when mapping 1D indices to 2D coordinates.
